title: Memory Characteristics and the SRAM-DRAM Split
unit: Memory Interfacing, Hierarchy and Cache Mapping
quickIdea: Every memory is described by the same five numbers - capacity, unit of transfer, access time, cost per bit and volatility - and the two RAM technologies differ sharply on the last three, which is why cache is SRAM and main memory is DRAM.
remember: Capacity = number of addressable locations x size of a location. A 4K x 16 memory holds 4096 locations of 2 bytes.
Unit of transfer = the number of bits moved at one time, set by the data-bus width, not by the address width.

Access time is the delay from presenting the address to having the data; cycle time is the minimum interval between two accesses to the same memory and is the larger of the two for DRAM, which must recover.
SRAM stores a bit in a latch, needs no refresh, and is fast and expensive; DRAM stores a bit as charge on a capacitor, must be refreshed, and is slower and far cheaper per bit.
Volatile means the contents are lost when power is removed; SRAM and DRAM are volatile, ROM, flash and disk are not.

example.prompt: A memory chip is described as 1K x 4. How many address lines and data lines does it need, and how many bits does it hold?
example.work: 1K = 1024 locations, so 10 address lines. Each location is 4 bits, so 4 data lines. Capacity = 1024 x 4 = 4096 bits.

gateAngle: GATE uses these definitions as the input to chip-count and decoder questions: the number of address lines a chip needs is log2 of its word count, and the number of data lines is its word width. Reading a chip's description wrongly makes every later step wrong.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: A 4K x 16 memory is built from 1K x 4 chips. How many address lines does each chip take, and how many chips are needed?
variations.answer: 10 address lines per chip (1K words); 4 chips side by side for the 16-bit width and 4 rows for the 4K depth, so 16 chips.
variations.why: It joins the chip description to the two-dimensional build, which is the arithmetic GATE actually asks for.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why does DRAM need refresh while SRAM does not?
variations.answer: DRAM holds a bit as charge on a capacitor, which leaks; the cell must be read and rewritten periodically. SRAM holds the bit in a latch that keeps its state as long as power is on.
variations.why: The refresh requirement is why DRAM has a cycle time longer than its access time and why a refresh interval can be part of a performance question.

trap.what: Confusing access time with cycle time.
trap.why: Access time is the latency of one read; cycle time is the minimum spacing between the starts of two accesses and includes recovery or refresh, so it is never smaller.
trap.counterexample: A DRAM with a 50 ns access time may need 70 ns between two accesses to the same bank: a sequence of dependent reads runs at cycle time, while independent reads to different banks can overlap at access time.

check.question: A chip holds 2^14 locations of 8 bits. What are its address and data widths, and how many bytes does it hold?
check.explanation: The address width is log2 of the location count; the data width is the location size; the capacity in bytes is the product divided by 8 bits per byte.
